title: Witnesses Say Tiger Victim Posed for Photos, Danced Before Entering Enclosure
excerpt: Witnesses say the man asked a stranger to photograph him with the tiger Altai in the background minutes before climbing over the barrier at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.
body:
• Witnesses now say the man posed for photos with Altai the tiger in the background and was dancing with his EarPods in moments before entering the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park on Saturday.
  • Del Taylor, a fellow visitor, says she took the man's phone and photographed him; audio her partner recorded of the exchange — "Can you grab a shot of myself with the tiger?" — has been viewed more than 3.2 million times on X.
  • The man, described as in his early 20s and unidentified, climbed over a metre-high viewing barrier at about 1:35 p.m. Saturday and was pronounced dead at the scene despite emergency response.
  • The park says the five-year-old Amur tiger will not be euthanized and is "safe and well"; the park closed for the weekend as South Yorkshire Police investigate.

Witnesses who stood near the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park on Saturday have described how the man who died after entering the pen with an Amur tiger appeared happy and relaxed in the minutes before he climbed over the barrier — asking a total stranger to photograph him with the animal behind him.

Del Taylor, who was watching the five-year-old Siberian tiger Altai from a viewing platform, told The Sun that the man approached her and asked: "Can you grab a shot of myself with the tiger?" She said she took his phone and photographed him, positioning the camera so Altai was visible in the frame with him. In audio captured by her partner, the man can be heard laughing as he asks for more pictures: "One more, one more, one more," before saying, "Thank you, lady."

Another visitor, Marie Miller, wrote on Facebook that she had seen the man "on the bridge with his EarPods in dancing," apparently enjoying the sight of the tiger sitting calmly in the sunshine. "He obviously wasn't with anyone and he asked a total stranger to take a picture of him with the tiger in the background," she wrote. "I honestly do think he just wanted to play with the tiger." Audio footage posted by Alex K Phillips on X, captioned as the man's final minutes, has been viewed more than 3.2 million times.

Context & Background

The man, described as being in his early 20s and who has not been publicly identified, was reported to have been at the park near Doncaster, northern England, on Saturday afternoon. According to witness accounts, after leaving the viewing platform he climbed over a metre-high viewing barrier at the park's "Land of the Tigers" habitat and dropped into the enclosure, landing on the grass a few feet from Altai.

Police and paramedics were called at about 1:35 p.m. Footage showed the tiger biting and clawing at the man as he sat on the grass trying to fend off the attack. One visitor said a woman tried to pull the man back on the platform but "wasn't strong enough." Emergency staff reached the scene and tried to drive the tiger off, with one witness reporting that staff fired two shots into the ground. South Yorkshire Police said: "The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury. Emergency services attended and sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene." The man's family has been informed and is being supported by specialist officers.

Altai arrived at Yorkshire Wildlife Park from Norway's Dyreparken zoo in February 2025 to join the female Tschuna as part of a European endangered-species breeding programme. The two-acre "Land of the Tigers" habitat features woodland, grassland and a waterfall pool.

""I honestly do think he just wanted to play with the tiger." Audio footage posted by Alex K Phillips on X, captioned as the man's final minutes, has been viewed more than 3.2 million times."

Impact & Analysis

The accounts reframe what is known about the seconds before the tragedy. Rather than a confrontation, witnesses describe a visitor who seemed to treat the predator as a backdrop — a pattern wildlife safety experts have flagged repeatedly in selfie-related incidents at animal attractions worldwide. The viral audio has sharpened public attention on how quickly fascination can turn fatal when barriers are breached.

The park placed a black screen around the enclosure after the attack and closed for the remainder of the weekend. In its statement, Yorkshire Wildlife Park said its emergency response procedures were immediately activated, adding: "We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened. The safety and wellbeing of our visitors, staff and animals remain our highest priority." The park also confirmed that Altai "is safe and well and will not be euthanized as a result of this incident," a decision police echoed, confirming the animal was uninjured and remained in its enclosure.

Diaspora Angle

This is a global story, but it lands in a country where many Indian families spend weekends at wildlife parks — a reminder for parents and caregivers that viewing barriers exist for a reason and that young visitors should never be left unsupervised near large-animal enclosures.

What's Next

South Yorkshire Police are leading the investigation into how the man entered the enclosure, working with the park and local authorities. The park has not yet said when it will reopen to the public. The man's identity has not been released; an inquest process is expected to follow once the police investigation concludes. Read our earlier report on the fatal incident.

Sources: New York Post, The Sun
